summary: Leftnotlost is a project by Houston, We-Xperts, from Doan Thi Diem Secondary School. It tells the story of NASA’s Lunar Roving Vehicles, electric cars that Apollo astronauts drove on the Moon. Boeing built the first rover in about 17 months, and it first drove on the Moon on July 31, 1971, during Apollo 15. The rovers carried tools for talking to Earth, finding the way and collecting rocks. They took astronauts to distant craters and mountains. Each rover weighed about 210 kg, so it was left behind to make room for moon samples. Our website lets visitors explore this story with charts, maps and a timeline, all based on NASA sources.
details:
Our website, LeftButNotLost is an interactive presentation about the Lunar Roving Vehicle, the electric car that Apollo 15, 16 and 17 astronauts drove on the Moon in 1971 and 1972. The three rovers were left behind when the crews flew home, so the project asks why, and shows how much they made possible.

Viewers move through seven slides covering how the rover was built, an interactive chart of the distance each mission drove (click a mission to see each moonwalk), lunar maps with the EVA routes, a reveal-the-answer question, and a clickable timeline. The goal is to help students and space fans explore a lesser-known part of Apollo, and to show that the rovers and their tracks are still part of the story of human exploration. NASA sources are linked at the end.

We built it as one self-contained web page using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and inline SVG, with no frameworks. Images are embedded, so it works offline on any device with a browser.

It’s creative because it works like an exhibit rather than a standard slide deck. Slides animate in, the moon floats against a starfield, and viewers can click into the chart, maps and timeline. We focused on accuracy, keyboard and screen-reader accessibility, and a layout that adapts from phone to widescreen.
